title: The shell exposes the accessible-defaults palette hook (light and dark) and accepts elicited operator overrides
iWant: the render shell to ship a light and dark categorical palette matched against WCAG contrast and to accept my brand tokens as overrides
soThat: the ratified palette is the recommended default and brand overrides remain contrast-safe when I feed them in (ADR-1902)

acceptanceCriteria.description: Given a rendered chart on a light background, every series colour and every axis text carries a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1 against its background (WCAG 1.4.3 for text; the 3:1 non-text contrast under WCAG 1.4.11 for series marks). The shell ships light and dark palettes matched against these ratios; the shell's palette accessor returns the applied palette by name and version. This AC is a build-scan surface (palette values readable from the applied blueprint's palette module); the pack has no dedicated check for it and the README names the gap under known mechanism-reach gaps as a build-scan opportunity for a v1.1 minor bump. Applying agent sets: the project-specific bindings, routes, thresholds, budgets, and names named in the assertion.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a rendered chart under either the light or dark palette
acceptanceCriteria.then: series colours meet WCAG 1.4.11 (3:1 non-text contrast) and axis text meets WCAG 1.4.3 (4.5:1) against the applied background

acceptanceCriteria.description: Given the shell's palette API, an operator supplies brand tokens (a palette override object keyed by series index or role) and the shell renders the operator palette; when the operator palette misses a token the shell falls back to the accessible-defaults palette at the same index and records a warning on the render log. The API surface (`renderShell({ palette, chart })`) is a project-side contract; the fallback behaviour is exercised by the applying project's own tests, not this blueprint's pack. Applying agent sets: the project-specific bindings, routes, thresholds, budgets, and names named in the assertion.
acceptanceCriteria.given: an operator palette with missing tokens
acceptanceCriteria.then: missing tokens fall back to the accessible-defaults palette and a warning is recorded

acceptanceCriteria.description: Given a rendered chart on a dark background, when the pack captures every series colour and text colour on the chart, each pair meets the WCAG 1.4.3 4.5:1 text contrast and WCAG 1.4.11 3:1 non-text contrast ratios against the dark background; the check runs the same colour-contrast calculation against the applied theme's background and fails on any pair under the threshold.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a rendered chart on a dark background
acceptanceCriteria.then: every series colour and text colour pair meets WCAG 1.4.3 (4.5:1 text) and WCAG 1.4.11 (3:1 non-text); a failure fails the pack

acceptanceCriteria.description: Given an operator-elicited palette override that names N brand tokens for N series but leaves M > N series unpaletted, the shell falls back to the accessible-defaults palette for the unpaletted series at the same index and the render log records exactly one warning per unpaletted series naming the missing token; a shell that silently substitutes without a log entry fails the pack check per ADR-1902.
acceptanceCriteria.given: an operator palette override that undersupplies for the series count
acceptanceCriteria.then: the unpaletted series fall back to the accessible-defaults palette at the same index and one render-log warning per unpaletted series names the missing token

acceptanceCriteria.description: Given a rendered chart whose applied theme background differs between light and dark modes, when the theme flips at runtime (a user toggles the theme), the palette applied to the chart re-resolves from light-defaults to dark-defaults automatically and the render log records the palette flip; a chart whose palette does not re-resolve on theme flip fails the pack check.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a rendered chart under a runtime theme flip from light to dark
acceptanceCriteria.when: the pack inspects the re-rendered chart
acceptanceCriteria.then: the palette re-resolves to the dark-defaults automatically and the render log records the flip
